headline: Nasdaq-100 closes down 0.98% mid-range after a two-way session, keeping Tail at 8 while a memory-led chip de-rating holds Stress elevated
body:
The defining fact of this hour is how the session ended rather than how far it fell. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed at 29,023.18, down 285.68 points or 0.98%, inside a 28,875.97-29,151.97 range. That close sits about 147 points above the session low and 129 below the session high, which is close to the middle of the day's range. Across the afternoon the index fell to its low, recovered, printed a marginal new high at 29,151.97, faded again and then settled without breaking down into the bell. A tape that repeatedly rejects its own extremes and finishes mid-range is the structural opposite of the persistent no-retracement path the Tail measure is built to detect, so Tail is scored 8.

The composition of the decline reinforces that reading. The Dow closed up 0.26% while the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.76% and the S&P 500 slipped 0.28%. Within the index, five of the eight tracked megacaps finished higher, with Meta up 1.66%, Amazon up 1.33%, Alphabet up 0.94% and Microsoft up 0.84%, while all seven tracked semiconductor names finished lower: Micron down 5.83%, AMD down 3.49%, Intel down 3.12%, Nvidia down 2.91% in a seventh consecutive decline and Broadcom down 2.63%. That is rotation inside the index, not the broad simultaneous de-risking that produces one-way index structure.

Cross-assets refuse to confirm a stress path. VIX closed at 15.84, up 4.69% on the day but inside a 15.61-16.06 range and low in absolute terms against a semiconductor complex down roughly 3% on average. The 10-year yield eased 2.9 basis points to 4.707% and the 30-year fell 4 basis points to 5.24%, though the 10-year remains close to the 20-month high of 4.75% set in the previous session, while the 2-year was essentially unchanged at 4.24%. Most notably, crude fell rather than spiked after the US announced a new sanctions campaign against Iran: WTI is 84.93, down 2.45%, and Brent 91.98, down 2.56%. A geopolitical headline that moves oil in the opposite direction to the risk it implies is not producing market transmission.

Stress stays at 45 in the elevated band because the underlying driver is unresolved. The memory-cost story behind the chip de-rating is a margin question for the whole AI hardware chain, and it arrives two days before a stack that combines the 12:30Z Core PCE and second-estimate GDP block on Wednesday with Nvidia's results after that session's close. Elevated Stress alongside a low Tail is the intended reading: a difficult, headline-heavy tape that has so far kept giving price back in both directions.

Delayed cross-asset context collected at 20:13Z is consistent with the verified close, showing Nasdaq futures down 0.96%, S&P down 0.29%, Dow up 0.24%, crude down 2.37% and Treasury futures modestly bid across the curve. That context is supporting evidence only. CME equity futures are in their daily 20:00Z-21:00Z maintenance halt, so no live forward price path exists at this moment; the published danger window therefore sits on tomorrow's 13:30Z cash open and the 14:00Z confidence and housing releases rather than on the current hour.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment. Through the 23 August evening Tail sat at 4 with Stress at 44-45 in a normal mode, then stepped to 15 at 22:00Z as Asian technology began repricing the memory-cost story before settling into a 7-12 band overnight with Stress easing to a window low of 38. The window's structural peak came in the European and early US hours: Tail reached 19 at 07:00Z with Stress at 58 in a trend-down mode as Europe priced the memory complex lower, eased to 11-13 in a mixed mode through the European morning, then moved to 20 at 13:00Z ahead of the cash open and to the window's only non-green slot, 26 with Stress 60 in a trend-down mode, at 14:00Z. From 15:00Z the series decayed steadily as the opening move failed to extend, running 13, 10, 9, 8 and 9 through the afternoon with Stress falling from 54 to 45 and Confidence rising to 87-88. Every slot outside 13:00Z and 14:00Z mapped to EA_ON.
outlookSummary: The conditional path stays inside the low Tail band for all 24 hours, so every slot maps to EA_ON. It opens at 8 for the 20:00Z cash close and futures maintenance halt, eases to 7 at the 21:00Z futures reopen, then lifts through the Asian hours to the overnight peak of 10 at 00:00Z, where Tokyo and Seoul price the memory-cost story most directly. The series returns to the horizon floor of 7 at the 04:00Z Asian close and the 05:00Z inter-session gap, which also carries the lowest conditional Stress at 40. It lifts to 11 at the 07:00Z European cash open, the weakest hour before the US session, then settles at 9-10 through the European morning. The horizon peak is 16 at 14:00Z, covering the US cash open at 13:30Z and the CB Consumer Confidence and New Home Sales releases at 14:00Z; that hour carries the danger window and the highest conditional Stress at 53. The series then decays to 13, 11 and 10 through the US afternoon before lifting to 11 at the 19:00Z power hour as positioning builds into Wednesday's Core PCE and GDP block and Nvidia's results after that session's close. Confidence declines from 88 to 70 across the horizon as verified evidence gives way to conditional assumption.
